modelNote: Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad and every co-op it has a documented tie to, cut from the Co-ops of Whatcom County graph (Marc Pierson’s layout). Ties are sourced; see each edge note.

legendEntries.label: Built or helped build the co-op

nodes.note: 1319 Cornwall Ave, Suite 101, Bellingham (moved from 203 W Holly St; Mount Vernon office too). Founded 2003 by Rosalinda Guillén. Food-sovereignty and farmworker organisation; develops farmworker co-ops. foodjustice.org.
nodes.label: Community to Community (C2C)

props.people: Rosalinda Guillén — Founder, lead strategist; Liz Darrow — Participatory Democracy Program Coordinator

nodes.note: 1240 Central Rd, Everson. Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm, launched 2017 on 65 acres. Berries, squash, nopales. $55,000 from the Community Food Sovereignty Fund (Food Lifeline) for a greenhouse; PCC Food Access Grant. Buyers include the Community Food Co-op, Skagit Valley Food Co-op, Bellingham Food Bank, Bellingham School District.
nodes.label: Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad

props.contactCaveat: No website of its own; reach through C2C

nodes.note: Downtown store 1220 N Forest St; Cordata store 315 Westerly Rd. Founded 1970 in Fairhaven. Runs the Farm Fund — since 2000 over $878,000 to 164 local food and farm projects, including tools for the forming Nooksack Tool Co-op (2016–19). Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Community Food Co-op

props.address: 1220 N Forest St and 315 Westerly Rd, Bellingham
props.people: Lisa Sedlar — CEO; Lydia Cox — Marketing & Outreach Director; Annabelle Rosborough — Board Administrator

edges.note: Farm Fund grant — co-op development for farmworkers — Listed in the Farm Fund's earlier projects: funded Community to Community's work "on cooperative development for farm workers and Latino consumer access to local food". Year not given.
edges.label: Farm Fund grant

edges.note: Organised and incubated the co-op; led the land fundraising — C2C organised Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm and raised grants, public funds and private donations to buy the 65 acres; the land is meant to pass to a land trust. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.
